issue.title: BUG: read_csv with usecols raises IndexError in low-memory mixed-dtype warning path
issue.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import csv
import pandas as pd

file = "repro.csv"

N_COLS = 87
N_ROWS = 20000
TARGET_POS = 50
TARGET_COL = "Overall_Judgment"
SWITCH_ROW = 8192

columns = [f"col_{i}" for i in range(N_COLS)]
columns[TARGET_POS] = TARGET_COL

with open(file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerow(columns)

    for i in range(N_ROWS):
        row = ["x"] * N_COLS

        if i < SWITCH_ROW:
            row[TARGET_POS] = "YES"
        else:
            row[TARGET_POS] = ""

        writer.writerow(row)

pd.read_csv(file, usecols=[TARGET_COL])
```

### Issue Description

On pandas 3.0.5, read_csv raises an internal IndexError when usecols selects a
column that is not at position 0 in the original CSV and different low-memory
chunks infer different dtypes for that column.

In the reproducible example above, the selected column contains strings in the
first low-memory chunk and only missing values in later chunks.

The traceback ends with:

    File "pandas/io/parsers/c_parser_wrapper.py", line 361, in _concatenate_chunks
        warning_columns.append(column_names[name])
                               ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
    IndexError: list index out of range

Changing only TARGET_POS from 50 to 0 makes the IndexError disappear. In that
case, read_csv succeeds and emits the expected DtypeWarning instead.

The following workarounds also succeed:

- low_memory=False
- explicitly specifying dtype for the selected column
- engine="python"

This suggests that the failure occurs in the low-memory mixed-dtype warning path
when usecols is used for a column whose original position is greater than 0.

### Expected Behavior

read_csv should successfully return the selected column.

If different low-memory chunks cause mixed dtype inference, pandas may emit a
DtypeWarning, as it does when the selected column is at position 0, but it
should not raise an internal IndexError.
